prediction.likelyOutcome: Likely a jury verdict well above the commissioners' $817,589.59 award but far below Appellant's $4.93-5.5M figures, given the serious credibility problems with the 2011 tax-credit-driven comparable sale and competing, substantive evidence on hotel-conversion feasibility; a verdict in the low-to-mid seven figures is the most probable range, with real variance depending on which highest-and-best-use theory the jury credits.

issues.label: Fair Market Value at Date of Taking (Competing Appraisals)

figures.label: Appellant's appraiser (Spence) valuation
figures.quote: Spence testified the fair market value of the Property at the time of the taking was $4.93 million

figures.label: LCRA's appraiser (Neff) valuation
figures.quote: the fair market value of the Property at the time of the taking was $573,000 and the Property's highest and best use was as a warehouse

issues.label: Reliability of the 2011 Sale as a Comparable (Tax-Credit Sham Structure)

figures.label: 2011 sale price used as comparable
figures.quote: NorthSide Regeneration, LLC ("NSR"), a company owned by Paul McKee, for $3.75 million in 2011

figures.label: Actual payments received before unwind
figures.quote: Appellant testified he received $733,000 from NSR as of March 2013

issues.label: Highest and Best Use: Boutique Hotel vs. Warehouse
Date-of-Taking Valuation Rule vs. Post-Taking Condition Evidence

figures.label: AT&T settlement payment
figures.quote: he paid AT&T $65,000 to resolve any claims arising from the termination of AT&T's lease with Appellant due to the Property's condemnation

outcome.description: After a seven-day jury trial in May 2018 the jury awarded $573,000, the value given by LCRA's appraiser and $244,589.59 below the commissioners' $817,589.59 award (the owner's appraiser said $4.93 million); the court denied a post-trial homestead allowance and taxed $21,207.13 costs against the owner. The Eastern District affirmed on April 21, 2020.

source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the Factual and Procedural Background: Pre-Trial (condemnation filing, commissioners' award, exceptions) and Trial (each side's evidence, including both appraisers). Removed: the Introduction (judgment amount and costs), the judge-assignment/recusal motions, footnotes 1-4 and one footnote marker, the 'Jury Verdict and Homestead Allowance' section and everything after it. LCRA's appraiser's figure, which the jury adopted, is retained as a party's stated position, so amountIsTheRequestedAmount is true. The building was zoned industrial; the owner's post-verdict homestead (primary-residence) claim was denied and is not part of the input.
